title: White musicians and Manetta teaching Dixieland
summary: White musicians did not sit in locally but followed the dances; Manetta in New Orleans taught many white players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: around here ever came in and then sat on your combos and their playing for these various dances? No, they didn't. Not out here. Well, how did these white musicians that like jazz, like Dixieland, show their interest in this? They would come to the dances in different places and listen. They would follow you around in from one place to another. Yes. Do you recall the names of any of the outstanding colored musicians that are in this area or in New Orleans who worked with white musicians to teach them how to play Dixieland? Do you know any of those? Emanuel Manetta in New Orleans. He taught quite a few. Emanuel Manetta. 된 !
